title: Switching a long recording to Edit mode draws its first frame without a hitch
goal: On a five minute recording with captions, pressing Cmd-2 (or any edit key) to go from View to Edit spends about 180 ms building the panel, the tool bar and the timeline in one frame, so the slide-in visibly stutters before it starts. Short recordings are fine. Make the switch smooth on long ones too.
notes: Found by view-mode-and-edit-mode-a-recording-opens-to-wat, 2026-09-28. Repro: a walk with openLongRetinaTalk, captionsWaitForThemselves, then key cmd+2 / wait 0.8 / cmd+1 / wait 0.8 repeated. Log: 'command+2 ... wait 0.8s, never went quiet ... busiest 215.4ms; mainBusy 814.6ms over 239 passes, longest 184.9ms' and the second switch 'longest 173.3ms'; Cmd-1 back to View is fine (longest 36 ms). sample(1) during six switches: main thread time is almost all SwiftUI NSHostingView.layout -> ViewGraph render / DisplayList update / AccessibilityNode.updateFocus, with InspectorPanel.body, PanelFieldRowLayout.sizeThatFits, TimelineTrackRow.body, CaptionStylePreview, VideoKit.TileGrid (transition tiles) on top. Ideas: keep the panel in the tree but off screen in View (check playback cost), defer the transitions tile grid a frame, stagger panel vs tracks. The ninety-second-cut walk now presses Cmd-2 before Q with no longestUnderMS on that wait.
acceptance: On the long captioned sample (openLongRetinaTalk), every wait after Cmd-2 reports its longest pass under 100 ms
View mode playback is no slower than it is today (the fix must not keep the panel updating while hidden if that costs playback frames)
the-ninety-second-cut-walk can put longestUnderMS 150 on the wait right after its Cmd-2
